subject: On-Prem Connectivity: Latency Commitments & Tunnel Design — Recap
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-retail.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: infra@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's demo — on-prem perf questions

Thanks for the demo today, Ben — useful overview. A couple of follow-ups from our infra team so we can validate whether an on-prem deployment will meet our latency SLAs:  

- Target P95 inference latency <= 120ms for 512-token generation (interactive).
- Sustained concurrency target: 80 simultaneous streams (we plan to burst to 150 for promotions).
- Streaming support required (token-level stream to browser).
- Network path: our edge PoP -> customer data center -> your private endpoint. We currently peer via AWS Direct Connect and have an active VPN fallback.

Attaching a simple network diagram and our rough internal latency budgets per hop. Please confirm if Redwood needs any special routing (GRE/UDP) or will accept TLS over TCP. Also: any egress requirements/observability hooks we should plan for?

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 30-min call if helpful.

— Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

Attachment: acme_network_diagram_v2.png (image/png)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-retail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — on-prem perf questions

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the diagram, very helpful. High-level responses below; I'm looping in Vivek (networking/infra) and Lauren (solutions) for the implementation details and concrete numbers for your topology. Quick summary:  

- Latency: 120ms P95 for 512 tokens is within scope for many of our on-prem customers when they place the Redwood private endpoint inside the same DC or across a low-latency Direct Connect link. We typically see 60–90ms server-side token latency on A100-class hosts for similar models, but network hop budgets matter.
- Concurrency/throughput: 80 sustained streams is fine; for bursts to 150 we recommend a small burst pool and autoscaled workers. We'll propose a capacity plan after we confirm average tokens/sec and tokenization profile.
- Streaming: supported. We stream token deltas over TLS (HTTP/2 or SSE); no special UDP/gRE required.
- Routing: TLS over TCP (mutual TLS optional) is the standard. We support IP allowlist, peering via Transit Gateway/Direct Connect, and VPNs as fallback.
- Egress: by default outbound connections are minimal — we recommend a dedicated NAT path if you need explicit egress accounting. We can also send telemetry to your on-prem observability collector.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Vivek to review your diagram and respond with recommended tunnel/peering config and expected one-way/internal hop budgets.
2) Acme to share tokenization profile / sample prompt size distribution (P50/P95 tokens per request).
3) Redwood to deliver a draft capacity plan and a short SLO appendix for the Private deployment.

I've attached our on-prem SLO checklist for your review. If that looks good, let's lock a 30-min sync with infra next week.

Best,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_onprem_slo_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-retail.com>, infra@acme-retail.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's demo — on-prem perf questions

Thanks for looping me in. Quick technical read:  

- Tunnel/Peering: Preferred = AWS Direct Connect + Transit Gateway peering to the private endpoint in Acme DC. Fallback = IPsec VPN with BGP. Both are supported. We recommend keeping MTU >= 1500 across hops to avoid fragmentation which spikes latency on token streaming.
- Protocols: Use TLS over HTTP/2 for streaming to minimize head-of-line blocking; SSE is acceptable if the client prefers. No UDP required.
- One-way budgets: If your internal budget is 40ms (edge -> app), we can usually get server-side P95 compute < 60ms for 512 tokens with quantized weights on T4/A10g-class hardware; combined path would be ~100ms P95 in well-provisioned setups. If you need to get below 100ms P95, we'd recommend colocating a small inference pool inside the same VLAN/tenant in your DC.
- Concurrency strategy: For 80 sustained streams and 150 burst, plan for concurrent model replicas with async batching disabled for latency-critical streams; we will set burst pool autoscaling thresholds and queue depth limits in the capacity plan.
- Observability: We'll export host-level metrics and span traces to your OTLP collector (TLS). We can also provide per-token latency breakdowns via the Redwood console for the private control plane.

Action for Acme: please confirm internal hop budgets per your diagram (edge -> load balancer -> redwood endpoint -> model host). Also share average tokens/sec per stream during interactive sessions. I can draft a recommended peering config and a sample CloudFormation/TF snippet for Direct Connect.

— Vivek
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-retail.com>

Cc: infra@acme-retail.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Thanks Ben/Vivek — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications and the next items from our side:  

- Our internal hop budgets (measured): edge -> LB = 12ms, LB -> app-router = 8ms, router -> host = 15ms. Total internal one-way = ~35ms. We'll attach trace samples from our load tests.
- Token profile: interactive chat avg 120 tokens (P50), P95 520 tokens. Peak tokens/sec per stream avg ~10 during demos.
- For Direct Connect we can provision a dedicated VLAN to your subnet; we prefer TLS over HTTP/2 and mutual TLS for auth.

Next steps we agree to:
1) I'll upload the trace samples and confirm Direct Connect VLAN details by EOD Monday.
2) Vivek to send the Direct Connect/Transit Gateway config snippet and the exact MTU/recommended queue depths.
3) Ben/Redwood to return a short SLO appendix (P50/P95 targets, concurrency guidance, fallback behavior) that we can include in our procurement packet.

If you can include an explicit statement about maximum expected P95 end-to-end latency (given our reported internal 35ms one-way) in the SLO appendix, that will help speed our procurement review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I'll schedule the 30-min follow-up for Tues.

— Elena
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Retail
